title: Java Multithreading & Concurrency
description: Progress from no concurrency experience to professional competence in Java multithreading — covering low-level thread mechanics, synchronization, high-level concurrency utilities, and modern virtual threads — sufficient to design, test, and debug concurrent full-stack applications.

nodes.label: Concurrency Prerequisites
nodes.description: Confirm the Java fundamentals — collections, lambdas, generics, exceptions — needed before concurrency, and recognize helpful supporting skills like JUnit, Mockito, and JDBC that later concurrency topics will build on.

nodes.label: Processes, Threads & Parallelism
nodes.description: Distinguish processes from threads from tasks, and separate concurrency (overlapping progress) from parallelism (simultaneous execution on multiple cores) while accepting that thread scheduling is inherently nondeterministic.

nodes.description: Track a thread through its NEW/RUNNABLE/BLOCKED/WAITING/TIMED_WAITING/TERMINATED lifecycle, and implement cooperative interruption and cancellation so long-running tasks can shut down cleanly.

nodes.label: Atomicity, Visibility & the Memory Model
nodes.description: Distinguish atomicity from visibility from ordering, and understand the Java Memory Model's happens-before relationship and safe publication as the rules governing what one thread is guaranteed to see of another's writes.

nodes.description: Prefer immutable objects and thread-confined state — including ThreadLocal — to eliminate synchronization needs entirely, following the principle that the best synchronization problem is shared mutable state that never existed.
